add.helpUncapped: Describe what he owes you. The appraiser sets the price — a coffee or a car, there’s no ceiling — and it starts earning interest immediately.
add.label: What does Kaikai owe you?
add.placeholder: He said he’d Venmo me for the pizza in March. He did not.
add.signInPrompt: Anyone can add to Kaikai’s debt — but every line says who added it, so you’ll need to sign in first.
add.title: Put something on his tab
ask.failed: The debt desk is not answering right now.
ask.label: Ask a question about Kaikai’s debt
ask.placeholder: What’s the stupidest thing he owes for?
ask.signInPrompt: The counter and the whole log are public. Asking questions runs a model, so that part needs an account.
ask.title: Ask about the debt
counter.clean: He owes nothing yet. Interest compounds at {{percent}}% a year on whatever gets logged.
counter.screenReaderClean: Kaikai owes nothing yet. Nothing is accruing.
counter.screenReaderRate: Kaikai owes approximately {{amount}}, growing by {{rate}} every {{unit}}. The figure updates continuously.
credit.chartDesc: A line chart of the credit score over the selected time window.
credit.gaugeDesc: A dial from 300 to 850 divided into five bands, with a needle at the current score.
credit.heroNote: Recomputed from the books against the clock, and about as steady as his finances. Everyone watching sees the same number at the same instant.
credit.hint: Recomputed continuously from the books, and about as stable as his finances. Everyone watching sees the same number at the same instant — it is a function of the clock, not a random walk in your tab.
credit.screenReader: Kaikai’s credit score is approximately {{score}}, rated {{band}}. It has moved between {{min}} and {{max}} over the last window. The figure updates continuously.
credit.title: Live credit score
credit.utilisationNote: Utilisation is measured against a notional $500 limit — a limit large enough for the ratio to ever fall under 100% is a limit nobody would extend to this borrower. Payment history is not an estimate: there is no repayment path in this system at all, so “never” is the literal state of the data.
credit.value.inquiries_one: {{count}}件が彼の名義で開設されました
desks.issuer.body: Structures and issues every instrument written against this balance. Each line on the tab below is originated here, priced at the appraiser’s mark, and placed on the books the moment it clears.
desks.issuer.name: RMH Capital — Debt Capital Markets
desks.ledeCapital: The tab is public, but the paper behind it is not self-issued. Two RMH Capital desks stand between a line in the log and the number at the top of this page.
desks.settlement.body: Books the repayments and carries the counterparty risk on a borrower whose balance has only ever gone one way. Anything Kaikai pays down settles through this team; so far it has had nothing to settle.
desks.settlement.nameCapital: RMH Capital — Counterparty Treasury & Risk Management
desks.title: Who issues it, who settles it
desks.workout: Neither desk works this out alone. Debt Capital Markets and Counterparty Treasury run the workout jointly — one marks the paper, the other marks the man behind it, and no restructuring clears without both. Kaikai has not been offered one.
log.emptyBody: Nothing itemised yet. Be the first to put something on his tab.
log.frontierWriting: You’ve outrun the archive. More of his history is being written right now — it’ll appear in a moment.
log.help: Every line he never paid, newest first. Keep scrolling and the ledger keeps digging — each receipt it recovers is saved for everyone who comes after you.
log.loadFailed: Could not read any further back.
log.title: Why he’s in debt
page.aiOffline: The appraiser is offline, so nothing new can be added or answered right now. The counter and the log below still work.
page.description: A live, compounding, permanently public record of everything Kaikai owes. Anyone can add to it. Nobody can pay it down.
page.title: The Kaikai Debt Counter
stats.accrual.desc: A line chart of the total debt over time, compounding continuously, with a dashed forward projection from the current balance.
stats.accrual.hint: Solid is history — everything logged by that month, compounded to that month. Dashed is the same curve run forward from today’s books, assuming nobody adds another thing.
stats.accrual.title: What he has owed, and what he will
stats.categories.desc: A ranked bar chart of the debt by category.
stats.categories.hint: Every category, ranked. Click a bar to filter the whole panel to it — the numbers, the other charts and the three spatial views all follow.
stats.categories.title: What he owes it on
stats.contributors.hint: Members who have added a line themselves, ranked by what those lines are worth now.
stats.contributors.title: Who put it there
stats.creditors.hint: Includes debts he ran up before anyone was counting — a recovered receipt names a real member as its creditor whether or not they ever logged anything.
stats.creditors.title: Who he owes the most
stats.distribution.desc: A histogram of individual debt amounts in log-spaced buckets.
stats.distribution.hint: Buckets are log-spaced, because the amounts are: the median line is a few dollars and the tail runs to whatever the appraiser felt like that day.
stats.distribution.title: How big a debt usually is
stats.empty: Nothing on the books yet — add a line and it appears here.
stats.error: The books would not open just now. The counter and the log are unaffected — try again in a moment.
stats.filter.title: Filter every chart
stats.globe.desc: A globe with the debt ledger plotted on it: categories by latitude, time by longitude, value by height. The same figures are in the table below.
stats.globe.hint: The whole archive on one sphere: latitude is the category, longitude is time, and each spike stands off the surface by what that bucket is worth. Drag to spin it — and poke it, it ripples.
stats.globe.legend: Newest month faces you at rest; the archive runs backwards round the far side. Faint spikes are on the hemisphere you cannot see yet.
stats.globe.title: The debt globe
stats.horizon.label: How far ahead to project
stats.hyper.desc: A four-dimensional scatter plot of the debt ledger, projected to the screen. The same figures are in the table below.
stats.hyper.hint: Each dot is one month of one category, placed in 4D by the four measures you pick, then projected twice to get here. Dots nearer along W are bigger and brighter. Drag to turn it in the ordinary planes; use the sliders for the three that have no ordinary equivalent.
stats.hyper.note: XY, XZ and YZ are the rotations you already know — they leave W alone. XW, YW and ZW trade a visible axis for the invisible one, which is why the shape appears to turn inside out without anything actually deforming.
stats.hyper.title: The ledger in four dimensions
stats.lede: Every figure below is a basis, not a total — the browser compounds it against the clock, so these charts keep growing while you read them, exactly like the counter at the top. Pick a category to filter everything at once.
stats.rhythm.desc: A heatmap of debt lines by day of the week and hour of the day, in UTC.
stats.rhythm.hint: Every line on the books by UTC weekday and hour. Darker means busier; an untinted cell means nothing has ever been logged in that hour.
stats.rhythm.peak_one: 最も忙しい時間：{{day}} {{hour}}:00 UTC（{{count}}行）
stats.rhythm.title: When it happens
stats.table.caption: Debt by category: compounded value, face value, line count and share.
stats.table.hint: The same figures the charts are drawn from. Colour is never the only thing telling you which row is which.
stats.table.title: Every number on this page
stats.tabsLabel: How to look at the books
stats.terrain.desc: A three-dimensional bar field of the debt by month and category. The same figures are in the table below.
stats.terrain.hint: Time runs left to right, the eight categories run back into the screen, and every column’s height is what that month of that category is worth right now. Drag to orbit it.
stats.terrain.title: The debt terrain (3D)
stats.tile.categoriesDetail: Categories he has managed to owe money in
stats.tile.giniDetail: 0 = every debt identical, 1 = one debt is all of it
stats.tile.interestDetail: {{share}} of what he owes never bought anything
stats.tile.linesDetail: {{rate}} a day across the whole archive
stats.tile.milestoneDetail: Solved from today’s books — nobody has to add a thing
stats.tile.rateDetail: Compounded continuously, forever, from the moment each line lands
stats.tile.spanDetail: Oldest recovered receipt to the newest line
stats.title: The books, in detail
stats.treemap.desc: A treemap where each category’s area is its share of the total debt.
stats.treemap.hint: Area is share of the compounded balance. Every tile is the same eight colours as everywhere else on this page; click one to filter.
stats.treemap.title: The pile, to scale
